obtained.how: the agency's own public ArcGIS feature services on MDIFW's ArcGIS Online organization ('MDIFW Black Bear Harvest by Town Feature', 'MDIFW Moose Harvest by Town Feature'), queried through the ArcGIS REST API on 2026-11-26 for Danforth, T8 R4 NBPP, Bancroft Twp and Weston. The responses were saved as JSON (MDIFW_nd-3.bear.json, MDIFW_nd-3.moose.json) and their attribute tables dumped to MDIFW_nd-3.harvest.txt. The service and item metadata are in MDIFW_nd-3.meta.txt

bibliography.quote: MDIFW Black Bear Harvest by Town from 2005-present

claims.claim: the 2019–25 black bear harvest ran 5–14 a year in Danforth
claims.location: web page (ArcGIS REST query), layer 0 BlackBearHistoricbyTown, attribute table, row TOWN 'Danforth', fields F2019–F2025
claims.conditions: annual harvest totals by town (bears registered as killed in the town; the service does not define the town further)

claims.claim: the 2019–25 black bear harvest ran 2–9 a year in T8 R4 NBPP
claims.location: web page (ArcGIS REST query), layer 0 BlackBearHistoricbyTown, attribute table, row TOWN 'T8 R4 NBPP', fields F2019–F2025

claims.claim: the 2019–25 black bear harvest ran 0–15 a year in Bancroft
claims.location: web page (ArcGIS REST query), layer 0 BlackBearHistoricbyTown, attribute table, row TOWN 'Bancroft Twp', fields F2019–F2025
claims.conditions: annual harvest totals by town; the service's name for it is 'Bancroft Twp'

claims.claim: Danforth's moose harvest fell from 9 a year (2009–10) to 0–1 a year (2019–25)
claims.location: web page (ArcGIS REST query), layer 1 MooseHistoricbyTown2022, attribute table, row TOWN 'Danforth', fields F2006–F2025
claims.conditions: annual moose harvest totals by town
claims.note: The numbers hold. The fall came at once, from 9 in 2010 to 1 in 2011, and 2009–10 were the series' peak (2006–08 were 8, 3, 4). Bancroft Twp shows the same pattern: 12 in 2009 and 2010, then 0–2 in 2019–25.

claims.claim: the fall in Danforth's moose harvest was 'driven by permits rather than density' (§3.8.4) / happened 'as permits were cut' (§2.9) (MDIFW harvest records)
claims.note: The services hold harvest counts only: no permits, effort or density. The permit explanation must rest on other sources (§3.8.4 cites Latti 2012: permits cut after the 2012 census). Note too that Danforth's drop came in 2011 (9 → 1), a year before that census.

notes: The 'project notes' compilation came from these two MDIFW services: every 2019–25 figure in the notes and the paper matches them. Both services are public (copyright and credits 'Maine Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife'). Their licence text says the data may not be redistributed without the Commissioner's permission, so quoting a few town totals is fine but the tables should not be republished whole. Created 25 March 2020; data updated 5 June 2026 (bear) and 11 March 2026 (moose); the bear layer covers 2005–2025 and the moose layer 2006–2025 (its item description says 2005). For context, Danforth's bear harvest in 2005–2018 was 9, 15, 7, 9, 7, 9, 11, 16, 6, 9, 2, 2, 6, 12, so 2019–25 is typical. Harvest totals by town count registrations; they are not a density and depend on hunter effort and access. Weston was also queried but is not used in the paper: bears 3, 4, 1, 2, 0, 3, 3 in 2019–25; moose 0–1. show.mjs matched every 'MDIFW n.d.' in §3.8 to this key. The paper cites these data as 'MDIFW harvest records' in §3.8.4 (lines 1141 and 1160); §2.9's sentence (01_…:401–403) repeats them without a citation.
